Navier–Stokes paper vs. Lean: Section 8 and Lemma 10.5 audit

Where the paper and its Lean formalization state things differently, extracted by a local model (3 independent samples per pair, kept separate) with every claim quoted and the quotes checked against the sources. This page lists differences. It does not say whether any difference matters. See METHODOLOGY.md. Paper: navier-stokes.pdf · Lean: openai/NavierStokesAndEuler at f9e8bc5b38b6

Validation against the two published discrepancies (Bastounis, Circelli & Hansen, arXiv:2610.08144): Lemma 8.6 (the paper loses m+4 derivatives, the Lean m+5) and eq. (10.19) inside the proof of Lemma 10.5 (the pressure-flux bound has a different first term). Lemma 8.6 and Lemma 10.5 were put on the target list because of that paper; no prompt mentions the discrepancies, the lemma, derivative counts or the bound.
  • Lemma 8.6: SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.inverse_finiteJets, 3/3 samples, SmoothFamilyTorusInverse.lean:868: The paper loses four derivatives, while the Lean declaration loses five.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 3/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:587-588: The algebraic structure of the first part of the bound differs between the two statements.
  • (10.19) in proof of Lemma 10.5: PressureFlux.exists_uniform_actual_pressure_flux_bound, 2/3 samples, R3/PressureFlux.lean:588: The Lean bound includes additional terms not displayed in the paper's estimate.
